title: Welcome to Ship by Sunday
goal: Set the contract: this is for completion, not consumption.
purpose: Reset the student's behavior. They need to feel guided, slightly challenged, and clear on what this weekend is actually for.
suggestedOpeningLines: Welcome to Ship by Sunday. This is not designed to be watched. It is designed to be completed.
I am going to show you what matters, then I am going to tell you to pause and go do the rep.
By the end of this sprint, you do not need to know everything. You need one finished rep.
beatsToCover: What this sprint is: structured, on-demand, one focused weekend.
What this sprint is not: a binge course, a bootcamp, a passive masterclass.
What they leave with: brief, spec, build, live URL.
The rule: do not skip ahead, do not hoard theory, do not wait to feel ready.
onScreen: You on camera.
Show the 4-block staircase graphic.
Flash the 4 end artifacts so the finish line feels real.
watchouts: Do not over-credential yourself here. Keep it crisp.
Do not explain every block in depth yet; just orient them.
suggestedClose: Good. Now you know the rules. Next, I will show you the full path so nothing feels mysterious.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Create a sprint folder and duplicate the provided templates / worksheets.
pausePrompt.comeBackWith: A ready workspace with all four worksheets open.

title: How the Sprint Works
goal: Show the sequence and remove uncertainty.
purpose: Give them the map before the climb. They should understand why each block exists and what breaks if they rush it.
suggestedOpeningLines: Each block solves a different problem, and each one sets up the next.
If you half-do the CEO Block, you pay for it in the Build Block.
This sprint works because we compress the right decisions, not because we cram in more content.
beatsToCover: CEO Block = choose the problem, customer, and scope.
Design Block = make the product concrete enough to build.
Build Block = use AI to implement the core product without spiraling.
Ship Block = deploy, share, and gather first feedback.
onScreen: Use the block diagram and put one artifact under each block.
If possible, show a bad example: vague idea -\> messy design -\> confusing build.
watchouts: Do not let this sound academic. Keep it tactical.
suggestedClose: Perfect. You know the path. Let's start with the first thing most people mess up: what to build.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Skim the 4 worksheets end to end.
pausePrompt.comeBackWith: A clear sense of what gets produced in each block.

title: Start With the Problem
goal: Get them out of feature-land and into pain-land.
purpose: Strong apps start with an annoying, expensive, or emotionally charged problem. Novelty is weaker than pain.
suggestedOpeningLines: Do not start with "I want to build an AI app." Start with "someone has this painful problem."
Pain creates urgency. Urgency creates value.
You are hunting for friction, not cleverness.
beatsToCover: Contrast weak starts with stronger problem statements.
Explain why personal pain is often the best starting point.
Give 2-3 examples from your own life or products.
onScreen: Whiteboard or notepad with 3 weak ideas and 3 stronger problem statements.
Show your own note-taking pattern if you have one.
watchouts: Do not let this become startup theory.
Do not drift into TAM or market size yet.
suggestedClose: You now have raw material. Next, we are going to choose one user, because vague users create vague products.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Write down 3 annoying problems from your life or work that would actually be worth solving, and name who has each one.

title: Pick One User
goal: Force specificity and constraint.
purpose: The student needs one user in one situation. Broad audiences kill speed.
suggestedOpeningLines: Not everyone. Not the whole market. One real user type in one real moment.
Specificity is not limiting; it is what lets you build something coherent fast.
A narrow user is easier to design for, easier to write for, and easier to test.
beatsToCover: Use the sentence: This app is for \_\_\_ who need \_\_\_ without \_\_\_.
Show a bad target and tighten it to something usable.
Explain the difference between a segment and a situation.
onScreen: Fill the user sentence live on screen.
If possible, show two variants and explain why one is sharper.
watchouts: Do not open up multiple personas.
Do not let them stack three user groups into one app.
suggestedClose: Good. Now we know who this is for. Next, define what changes for them if this works.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Complete the sentence "This app is for..." and lock one user.

title: Define the Outcome
goal: Translate features into transformation.
purpose: Students need to define the promised outcome so the product can be judged by a result, not a pile of features.
suggestedOpeningLines: People buy outcomes, not tools.
Your app is a machine for creating one better future state.
If you cannot say the result simply, the product is still foggy.
beatsToCover: Write one sentence that starts with: After using this, the user can...
Give weak feature-heavy examples, then rewrite them into outcomes.
Tie this outcome to what will be shown in the demo later.
onScreen: Show the before/after of weak vs strong promise lines on screen.
watchouts: Do not overpromise money or business results.
Keep the outcome grounded and demonstrable.
suggestedClose: Now we have the problem, the user, and the outcome. Next, we do just enough research to avoid building blind.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Write one user-facing outcome statement.

title: Light Research, Not a Thesis
goal: Gather signal without disappearing into research hell.
purpose: Students need pattern awareness, not a dissertation.
suggestedOpeningLines: You are not writing a market report. You are trying to understand how this gets solved today.
Look for existing solutions, user complaints, and repeated expectations.
Borrow patterns. Avoid blind reinvention.
beatsToCover: Show quick scans of Google, app stores, Reddit, or product sites.
Capture: what they do well, what they do poorly, what users seem to care about.
Keep the note format brutally simple.
onScreen: Screen-share a fast research pass and capture 3 short notes.
watchouts: Do not let this become competitor paralysis.
No long rants about strategy books.
suggestedClose: Good. You have enough signal. Now turn the product into a simple journey.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Find 2-3 existing solutions and write down what they do well, badly, and what users seem to care about.

title: Map the Core Flow
goal: Turn the app into a 5-7 step user journey.
purpose: This is where the product becomes navigable. If they cannot map it, they cannot design or build it cleanly.
suggestedOpeningLines: If you cannot explain the flow in 5 to 7 steps, it is probably too muddy.
Words and arrows are enough. This is a functional map, not a mural.
Beginning, middle, end.
beatsToCover: List actors if needed, but keep it light.
Write the ending first if that helps.
Focus on the critical moment where the product actually delivers value.
onScreen: Draw the flow live with simple boxes and arrows.
watchouts: Do not add edge cases too early.
Do not let them map three different products at once.
suggestedClose: Now we know the path. Last step: cut scope until this can actually ship.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Map the core flow in 5-7 steps using only words and arrows.

title: Kill Scope
goal: Prevent weekend death by feature creep.
purpose: The key behavior here is subtraction.
suggestedOpeningLines: A smaller shipped app beats a larger imaginary one.
Version one is not supposed to impress everyone. It is supposed to work.
What has to exist by Sunday? Everything else is later.
beatsToCover: Split features into: must-have, nice-to-have, definitely-not-now.
Define what good enough for Sunday means.
Cut at least three things live.
onScreen: Show the worksheet being tightened in real time.
watchouts: Do not let them hide bloat behind future-proofing.
Keep the win condition explicit.
suggestedClose: Great. You now have a brief. Next, we turn the idea into something concrete enough to build.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Fill out the MVP section and cut at least 3 things.

title: CEO Block Wrap-Up
goal: Lock the brief so the next block has real inputs.
purpose: This is the handoff from thinking to form.
suggestedOpeningLines: By now, somebody else should be able to understand what you are building in under 60 seconds.
If the brief is foggy, fix it now. It does not get cheaper later.
beatsToCover: Review the completed worksheet quickly.
Point to the problem, user, outcome, flow, and scope.
onScreen: Show the final one-page brief.
watchouts: Do not introduce new concepts here.
suggestedClose: Nice. The app now exists on paper. In the next block, we make it visible.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Complete Worksheet 01 fully.

title: Find References First
goal: Stop them from inventing from a blank brain.
purpose: Use reference gathering to reduce randomness and raise taste quickly.
suggestedOpeningLines: Do not design from a blank brain.
Steal structure, not identity.
References compress years of pattern exposure into minutes.
beatsToCover: Show where you actually look: Mobbin, Spotted in Prod, SaaS sites, apps, whatever you really use.
Capture both UX flow and visual tone.
Tell them what to notice: layout, hierarchy, motion, trust cues.
onScreen: Screen-share a fast reference hunt and drag 3-5 screenshots into one board.
watchouts: Do not let them scroll forever.
Do not let this become moodboard cosplay.
suggestedClose: Good. You have raw visual ingredients. Now sketch the product before software gets involved.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Gather 3-5 references close to your desired flow or look.

title: Sketch Before Software
goal: Get them using paper to remove ambiguity fast.
purpose: Sketching is speed. It forces decisions before the build starts lying to you.
suggestedOpeningLines: Paper is still one of the fastest ways to make an app less abstract.
Ugly sketches are fine. Vague prompts are not.
You are not making art. You are making decisions.
beatsToCover: Show boxes, arrows, rough controls, labels.
Use one core flow and sketch only the important screens.
If stuck, use a 6-up exercise and make six ugly variants fast.
onScreen: Overhead camera or a quick paper demo. Keep it raw.
watchouts: Do not over-teach sketching theory.
Do not apologize for roughness.
suggestedClose: Perfect. Now we string these moments into a sequence.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Sketch the core screens of your app on paper.
pausePrompt.comeBackWith: Rough paper sketches of the main screens.

title: Storyboard the Journey
goal: Turn sketches into an ordered experience.
purpose: This helps them think in scenes rather than isolated screens.
suggestedOpeningLines: A good storyboard reduces confusion before code starts.
Products are journeys, not just pages.
Sequence creates clarity.
beatsToCover: Start with where the user first encounters the product.
Move through the key task.
End on the outcome or completion moment.
onScreen: Lay the sketches or frames left to right and narrate the user moving through them.
watchouts: Do not explode into every edge case.
Keep the spine of the product visible.
suggestedClose: Now that the flow is clear, let us get just enough Figma under your fingers to move quickly.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Lay out the user journey screen by screen.

title: Figma Basics for Speed
goal: Remove friction around the tool itself.
purpose: Teach only the basics required to survive the sprint.
suggestedOpeningLines: This is not Figma school. This is enough Figma to keep the sprint moving.
Fluency matters because awkward tools slow decisions.
Practice beats explanation here.
beatsToCover: Show frames, move, duplicate, resize, align, and basic layout behavior.
Demonstrate the hotkeys you actually want them to practice.
Keep the file simple and repeatable.
onScreen: Screen-share the provided Figma file and do the hotkeys in rhythm.
watchouts: Do not show the whole Figma universe.
Do not drift into auto-layout philosophy unless it directly helps this sprint.
suggestedClose: Good. Now use the tool to translate the sketches into rough screens.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Open the provided Figma file and practice the core hotkeys until they feel less weird.
pausePrompt.comeBackWith: Basic comfort moving around the file.

title: Turn Sketches Into Rough Screens
goal: Create buildable roughs, not polished comps.
purpose: They need just enough fidelity that the build becomes translation instead of guesswork.
suggestedOpeningLines: Your job is clarity, not beauty.
Rough screens are enough if the hierarchy and flow are obvious.
AI builds better from concrete screens than from vibes.
beatsToCover: Build 3-5 key screens only.
Place content, controls, hierarchy, and basic labels.
Add small notes where something important needs explaining.
onScreen: Screen-share the creation of one rough screen from scratch.
watchouts: Do not chase pixel perfection.
Keep momentum higher than polish.
suggestedClose: Now give the product just enough style direction that it stops feeling generic.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Create rough versions of your main screens in Figma.

title: Choose a Visual Direction
goal: Set a simple visual system for the build.
purpose: Students need direction, not a giant brand package.
suggestedOpeningLines: You do not need a full brand system. You need a coherent direction.
Pick a feel, not fifty options.
A little taste goes a long way when the layout is already clear.
beatsToCover: Choose one type direction, one spacing feel, one UI vibe.
Define 3 simple style rules.
Tie those rules back to the references.
onScreen: Show quick before/after polish on a rough screen.
watchouts: Do not teach branding theory for 20 minutes.
Avoid unnecessary logo talk unless it matters to the flow.
suggestedClose: Great. The product is now concrete. Next, we turn this into working software.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Choose a visual direction and write 3 style rules.

title: Design Block Wrap-Up
goal: Lock the design spec before building begins.
purpose: This is the handoff from concept to implementation.
suggestedOpeningLines: When this block is done, building should feel like translation, not guessing.
If the key screens are unclear, fix them now.
beatsToCover: Review the reference board, screen list, rough frames, and style rules.
onScreen: Show the completed design spec / worksheet.
watchouts: Do not start coding here.
suggestedClose: Good. The build phase is next. We are done guessing.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Complete Worksheet 02 fully.

title: Build From the Brief
goal: Teach them to prompt from clarity, not vibes.
purpose: The model is only as useful as the instructions it gets.
suggestedOpeningLines: Do not prompt from vibes. Prompt from clarity.
Most AI builds fail before the code starts because the product is still foggy.
Your brief is the build's source of truth.
beatsToCover: Show the difference between a weak prompt and a strong brief-based prompt.
Explain what the agent needs: product, user, flow, scope, definition of done.
onScreen: Paste the brief into an agent template on screen.
watchouts: Do not ask the model to be creative where accuracy matters.
Do not overcomplicate the prompt structure.
suggestedClose: Nice. Now let us get the environment ready so you can actually run the thing.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Copy your product brief and design spec into the agent brief template.

title: Set Up the Environment
goal: Get the starter project running without wandering.
purpose: Students need one path, one repo, one local success state.
suggestedOpeningLines: Pick one path and move.
The goal is to see the app running locally, not to become an infrastructure engineer.
If setup is messy, the rest of the sprint gets emotionally expensive.
beatsToCover: Open the starter repo.
Run the commands.
Show the browser running the local app.
Point to the minimum folders that matter.
onScreen: Screen-share terminal + editor + browser.
watchouts: Do not compare five editors or three deployment providers.
Avoid rabbit holes on version control unless absolutely necessary.
suggestedClose: Good. Now you have a running shell. Next, brief the agent the right way.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Open the starter project and get it running locally in your browser.

title: Brief the Agent Correctly
goal: Teach controlled delegation.
purpose: The student must learn to direct the model step by step.
suggestedOpeningLines: The model needs constraints, sequence, and a definition of done.
Ask for one step at a time.
Review output like a product lead, not a spectator.
beatsToCover: Show how to request only the first screen or first flow step.
Show how to correct the agent when it drifts.
Emphasize iteration over one giant magic prompt.
onScreen: Real prompting on screen, not fake perfect examples.
watchouts: Do not imply the first output should be perfect.
Do not let them ask for the whole app at once.
suggestedClose: Great. The app has started. Now we build the spine end to end.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Use your brief to ask the agent to implement only the first screen or first step of the flow.

title: Build the Core Flow
goal: Implement the main path before edge cases.
purpose: This is the heart of the block.
suggestedOpeningLines: Build the spine first.
One screen at a time. One user path at a time.
If the core flow works, you are winning.
beatsToCover: Implement the main user path end to end.
Check handoff between screens.
Keep the success state visible.
onScreen: Show the flow working as it gets stitched together.
watchouts: Do not chase every edge case.
Do not drift into architecture theory.
suggestedClose: Good. Now let us stop bugs from eating the whole weekend.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Implement the main user flow end to end.
pausePrompt.comeBackWith: The core product flow working locally.

title: Debug Without Spiraling
goal: Keep them focused on blocker bugs.
purpose: This lesson protects morale.
suggestedOpeningLines: Not every bug matters equally.
Fix the things blocking the core flow first.
Good enough for Sunday is the standard.
beatsToCover: Show how to identify blocker bugs vs cosmetic bugs.
Use the agent to isolate and fix issues.
Explain what gets left for version two.
onScreen: Screen-share one or two real bug fixes.
watchouts: Do not let this turn into a debugging masterclass.
Stay ruthless about priorities.
suggestedClose: If the core flow works locally, you are ready to ship.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Fix the 1-3 issues blocking your core flow.
pausePrompt.comeBackWith: An app that works locally from start to finish.

title: Build Block Wrap-Up
goal: Lock the local milestone and prep for deployment.
purpose: This is the handoff from local product to public product.
suggestedOpeningLines: By now, the app should work locally even if it is still ugly.
Ugly and working is enough for the next block.
beatsToCover: Review the definition of done, blocker fixes, and what still does not matter yet.
onScreen: Show the local app completing the core flow.
watchouts: Do not start polishing forever.
Move them toward deployment.
suggestedClose: Nice. The product works on your machine. Next, it needs to leave your machine.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Complete Worksheet 03 fully.
pausePrompt.comeBackWith: A working local app and a completed agent brief.

title: Ship the Core, Not the Fantasy
goal: Mentally prepare them to launch imperfect work.
purpose: Most students stall here because they compare the current product to the dream product.
suggestedOpeningLines: Ugly and live beats beautiful and trapped.
Version one is supposed to prove the core, not satisfy every fantasy.
The question is simple: does the main promise work?
beatsToCover: Define the shipping checklist.
Separate critical from optional.
Show what good enough to ship looks like.
onScreen: On screen, make a short ship checklist.
watchouts: Do not feed perfectionism.
Do not turn this into brand polish hour.
suggestedClose: Good. Now we are going to get a URL, because that changes the psychology instantly.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Write down what must work before this app is allowed to ship.

title: Deploy the App
goal: Get the app live fast.
purpose: The student needs a public URL, not a deep lesson on infra.
suggestedOpeningLines: The goal is a URL, not infrastructure mastery.
Pick the simplest deployment path and move.
Verify the live app immediately.
beatsToCover: Walk through deployment.
Show environment variables only if truly needed.
Test the live URL and the core flow.
onScreen: Screen-share the deployment start to finish.
watchouts: Do not compare deployment platforms.
Keep the energy high once the URL appears.
suggestedClose: Nice. The app is live. Now make it easier to understand and easier to share.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Deploy the app and get a live link.

title: Record a Simple Demo
goal: Create a low-friction asset for sharing.
purpose: A short walkthrough makes the app real to other people quickly.
suggestedOpeningLines: A quick demo lowers confusion and increases response rate.
Show the flow, not your entire worldview.
Thirty to sixty seconds is enough.
beatsToCover: Use a simple script: problem, what it does, one core flow, outcome.
Keep the camera / narration optional if needed.
onScreen: Record a bare-bones demo on screen.
watchouts: Do not over-edit.
Do not turn this into content production class.
suggestedClose: Good. Now the product is easier to send. Next, actually send it.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Record a 30-60 second walkthrough of the core flow.

title: Send It to Real Humans
goal: Break the fear barrier and start feedback.
purpose: This lesson is about courage and momentum, not scale.
suggestedOpeningLines: You do not need fifty users today. You need five real sends.
Small distribution is still real distribution.
Feedback starts with exposure.
beatsToCover: Choose the first 5 people.
Use a simple outreach message.
Ask for confusion, friction, and usefulness - not compliments.
onScreen: Show the send list and the outreach script.
watchouts: Do not let them delay because they want a perfect landing page.
Do not ask vague feedback questions.
suggestedClose: Good. The product is in the world. Last step: capture what happens and choose version two intelligently.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Send the app to 5 people using the provided script.

title: Capture Feedback and Plan Version Two
goal: Turn first responses into direction.
purpose: This is where the sprint stops being a one-off and becomes a loop.
suggestedOpeningLines: Feedback is useful when it changes decisions.
Confusion beats compliments as a signal.
Version two should be chosen, not guessed.
beatsToCover: Log the first feedback.
Sort it into confusion, bugs, and opportunity.
Choose the top 3 improvements only.
onScreen: Show a simple feedback tracker and prioritization grid.
watchouts: Do not let them promise a full roadmap.
Keep it tight and actionable.
suggestedClose: That is the loop. You scoped it, designed it, built it, shipped it, and learned from it.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Log the first feedback you get and choose the top 3 improvements for version two.

title: Final Wrap
goal: Close the identity shift.
purpose: The student needs to feel the transformation in behavior, not just the completion of content.
suggestedOpeningLines: Most people never complete a full rep. You did.
The goal was never to know everything. The goal was to become someone who ships.
Now do it again with better instincts.
beatsToCover: Recap the 4 artifacts.
Name the rep they just finished.
Invite them to iterate, not disappear.
onScreen: Show all 4 artifacts side by side: brief, spec, build, live URL.
watchouts: Do not add new teaching here.
Make it feel earned and closed.
suggestedClose: Live beats stuck. Shared beats hidden. Finished beats almost.

pausePrompt.jobNow: Review all four worksheets and write down your next iteration date.
pausePrompt.comeBackWith: A clear plan for version two or the next app.
